multivariate.visible_excerpt: What the ordinary-start study found A frozen 200-seed Gaussian study used 60 pedigree animals, four traits, three complete records per animal, one genetic factor, trait intercepts and an estimated unstructured residual covariance. Each default and balanced start had a 5000-iteration limit. Of all 200 attempts, 141 converged and 110 met the predeclared covariance-recovery diagnostics. There were 59 nonconverged fits, 20 genetic-covariance error classifications and 11 residual-covariance error classifications. The diagnostic recovery fraction was 55%, with a Monte Carlo standard error of 3.52 percentage points and a Wilson 95% interval of 48.1%–61.7%. The study specified no overall pass cutoff. Near-uniqueness-floor flags occurred in 13 fits, including six classified as recovered; two fits had a better nonconverged start, including one classified as recovered. These flags remain in the counts. Treat returned values from a nonconverged fit as diagnostic output.
